parole.testo: Borrowed from Dutch Low Saxon [Term?]. Doublet of uier. In the past sometimes used in standard Dutch writing, particularly following its use by the seventeenth-century playwright Joost van den Vondel.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Dutch Low Saxon, equivalent to noaber + -schap; cognate of nabuurschap.
Popularized by the 1977 song Oerend hard by Dutch Low Saxon (Twents) rock band Normaal. Variant of oer-, in turn from German ur-.
Borrowed from Dutch Low Saxon vief.
